options: A plan — due dates, discount terms, and amounts expected once an invoice is validated
The supplier's bank account details
The invoice's distribution lines
A record that money has already been sent
questions.explain: A payment schedule is a plan that exists once the invoice is validated, regardless of whether any money has actually moved.

questions.q: Why is the invoice-to-payment relationship in AP_INVOICE_PAYMENTS_ALL described as many-to-many?
options: Because payments and invoices are stored in the same row
Because each invoice can only ever have one payment
Because a single invoice can be paid across multiple payments, and a single payment can cover multiple invoices
Because the table has no relationship to invoices at all
questions.explain: Partial payments over time, and batch payments covering several invoices at once, make this a genuine many-to-many relationship.

questions.q: Where is the actual physical payment document (check number, EFT reference) generated and tracked?
options: On AP_PAYMENT_SCHEDULES_ALL
In Oracle Payments, the IBY_ prefixed module
It is not tracked anywhere
On AP_INVOICES_ALL directly
questions.explain: Oracle Payments (IBY_) owns the physical mechanics of disbursement and is shared across products rather than being private to Payables.

questions.q: Which column in AP_INVOICE_PAYMENTS_ALL would you sum, filtered by INVOICE_ID, to find how much of an invoice has actually been paid?
options: SEGMENT1 on POZ_SUPPLIERS
PARTY_ID on HZ_PARTIES
INVOICE_AMOUNT on the header
AMOUNT applied in that specific invoice-payment pairing
questions.explain: Each row in AP_INVOICE_PAYMENTS_ALL records the amount applied for a specific invoice-payment pairing; summing those for one invoice gives the amount actually paid.

questions.q: Why is it risky to treat "scheduled," "applied," and "disbursed" as the same thing when answering "is this invoice paid"?
options: Scheduling always happens after disbursement
They are always identical in Oracle Fusion, so there's no risk
An invoice can be scheduled but not yet applied, or applied but not yet fully disbursed — collapsing the three into one answer can be wrong
Only "disbursed" exists; the other two states are fictional
questions.explain: Scheduled, applied, and disbursed are three distinct states tracked in different places, and an invoice can be in one state without yet being in another.
